FOREWORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Lubricants and Related Products Sectional Committee had beenapproved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. Non-soap grease is extensively used in the steel industry and other industries for lubrication. This standard is intended chiefly to cover the technical provisions relating to the supply of the non-soap grease and it does not include all the necessary provisions of a contract. This standard was published in 1989. In this revision non-soap grease suitable for bearing operating at temperature has been increased. In view of environmental concern grease of Grade 1 and Grade 2 molybdenum disulphide or graphite or mixture of them have been incorporated to get synergistic effect of molybdenum disulphide/graphite. Rust protection test has been made as pass instead of rating 1. Requirement of water resistance has been reduced to improve water resistance characteristic. Characteristic for pumpability test has been replaced by mobility test. Water spray off test has been included to evaluate water resistance in presence of water flow under pressure. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revise4'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Grade 1 and Grade 2 shall contain molybdenum disulfide or graphite or a combination thereof. 4 REQUIREMENTS 4.1 General The material shall be smooth and homogenous and free from objectionable odour and visible impurities and shall possess good pumpability characteristics. It shall be free from deleterious materials and fillers other than molybdenum disulphide, graphite or a mixture of them and shall not show any signs of breakdown, hardening or tendency of the constituents to separate. 4.2 Composition The material ingredients: a) b) c) shall consist of the following

5 PACKING AND MARKING 5.1 Packing The material shall be packed in metal or any other suitable containers as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 5.2 Marking 52.1 The containers shall be securely closed and marked with the following: i) Indication of source of manufacture; ii) Name and grade of material; iii) Net mass of material; 2

iv) v)

Recognized trade-mark, if any; and Identification in code or otherwise to enable the lot of consignment or manufacture to be traced back from records.

5.2.2 BIS Certification Marking Each container may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 5.2.2.1 The use of Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to

1
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 6 SAMPLING 6.1 Representative samples of the material shall be drawn as prescribed in IS 1447 (Part 3). 6.2 Number of Tests Individual containers selected according to IS 1447 (Part 3) shall be opened and examined for the general requirements given in 4.1. Tests for consistency shall be done on individual samples.

IS 12790 : 1999 6.2.1 Tests for all the remaining characteristics shall be done on the composite sample prepared by mixing small portions from individual containers selected in the sample. 6 3 Criteria of Conformity . The lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of this specification, if each of the containers selected satisfies the general requirements given in 4.1. For consistency and other requirements, the criteria for conformity given in IS 1447 (Part 3) shall be followed.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards PLt, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'.
